chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abi Wallad al-Hannat, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a mukatab whose master stipulated with him, when he made the contract of mukatabah with him, that if he committed an injury against a man—so he said:

If he has paid something of his mukatabah, he is held liable for his injury in proportion to what he has paid of his mukatabah, as one who is free. Then if anything of the liability for the injury remains beyond his ability, that is taken from the property of the master who made the mukatabah contract with him.

I said: What if the injury was against a slave? He said: Upon the like of that, he is handed over to the master of the slave whom the mukatab injured, and retaliation is not carried out between the slave and the mukatab if the mukatab has paid something of his mukatabah. But if he has not paid anything of his mukatabah, then retaliation is carried out for the slave from him, and the master is made liable whenever the mukatab commits an injury, because he is still his slave so long as he has not paid anything of his mukatabah.

key_terms.الْحُرِّ: A free person, as opposed to a slave.
key_terms.جَرَحَهُ: He wounded him or caused an injury to him.
key_terms.جِنَايَةً: A bodily injury or offense that entails legal liability.
key_terms.غُرِّمَ: He is made financially liable or charged compensation.
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: His master, the owner who entered into the mukatabah contract with him.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave under a contractual manumission agreement to purchase his freedom in installments.
key_terms.مِنْ مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: From his mukatabah payment obligation or contracted manumission amount.
key_terms.يُقَاصُّ: Retaliation or equal requital is carried out in legal retribution.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mukatab injures a free person or a slave before completing his mukatabah?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning the liability of a mukatab who commits an injury. His responsibility is tied to how much of his mukatabah payment he has completed, while the remaining liability may fall upon the master; if he has paid nothing, he remains in the legal status of a slave for such rulings.
